quick: With or without food, any time
Severe (not on HD): start 5 mg, max 10 mg
summary: Rosuvastatin is a high-potency statin that markedly lowers LDL-C and reduces cardiovascular events. Dosed 5-40 mg once daily. Asian patients and severe renal impairment require lower starting doses. Contraindicated in pregnancy and active liver disease.
indications: Reduce risk of major adverse CV events in adults at increased CV risk (age, hsCRP >=2 mg/L, plus one risk factor)
Primary hyperlipidemia in adults (adjunct to diet)
Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (adults and children >=8 years)
Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (adults and children >=7 years)

dosage.n: Usual start 10-20 mg; 40 mg reserved for inadequate response
Higher plasma levels; weigh risk above 20 mg

dosage.d: Start 5 mg, do not exceed 10 mg once daily

admin: Take orally once daily at any time, with or without food
May take with or 2 hours before an aluminum/magnesium antacid
Assess LDL-C as early as 4 weeks after start and adjust
Use lower start dose in Asian patients and severe renal impairment
moa: Competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, reducing hepatic cholesterol synthesis. This upregulates hepatic LDL receptors, increasing LDL uptake and catabolism, thereby lowering LDL-C, total cholesterol, ApoB and triglycerides while modestly raising HDL-C.

absolute: Acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis
relative: Predisposition to myopathy (renal impairment, hypothyroidism, age >65)

preg: Contraindicated. Discontinue when pregnancy is recognized; statin therapy during pregnancy provides no benefit and may harm the fetus.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding. Discontinue drug or nursing.
renal: No adjustment in mild-moderate impairment. In severe impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) not on dialysis, start 5 mg and do not exceed 10 mg once daily.
hepatic: Contraindicated in active liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevations. Monitor LFTs and use caution with alcohol or chronic liver disease.

major: Cyclosporine - markedly increased exposure; limit rosuvastatin to 5 mg/day
Gemfibrozil - increased exposure and myopathy risk; avoid or limit to 10 mg
Certain HIV/HCV protease inhibitors - dose limits apply
minor: Aluminum/magnesium antacids - reduced exposure if taken together; separate by 2 h
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol due to hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate transaminases, CK and cause dipstick proteinuria/hematuria (usually transient).

monitoring: Lipid panel at baseline and 4-12 weeks after start/change
Liver enzymes at baseline; repeat if indicated
Creatine kinase for unexplained muscle symptoms
counsel: Take once daily at any time, with or without food
Report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness
Separate antacids by at least 2 hours
Limit alcohol; continue diet and exercise
Do not use if pregnant or breastfeeding
pk: LDL reduction within 1 week, near-maximal by 4 weeks
Store at 20-25 C in original container, protect from moisture
pearls: Most potent statin per mg; 5-10 mg lowers LDL-C ~45-50%
Largely hydrophilic - less CYP3A4 metabolism than atorvastatin
Lower starting dose in Asian patients (higher plasma levels)
40 mg reserved for patients not at goal on 20 mg
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless close to the next dose; do not double up.
overdose: No specific treatment; manage symptomatically with supportive care. Hemodialysis does not significantly enhance clearance. Monitor for muscle and hepatic effects.
